What is the ratio of the total number of students in Section A whose height is less than 1.65 metres to the total number of students in Section B whose height is less than 1.65 metres
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Heights strictly less than 1.65 m are 1.55 m, 1.60 m, and 1.62 m.

Students in Section A = 5 + 9 + 11 = 25

Students in Section B = 4 + 8 + 13 = 25

Required Ratio = 25 : 25 = 1 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

A table containing the heights of students in two sections, A and B.

We need the ratio of students with heights less than 1.65 metres in Section A to Section B.

Ratio Comparison

A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind. It is typically expressed in its simplest form by dividing both components by their highest common factor.

Tabular Data Interpretation

When verifying conditions such as 'less than a value', you only aggregate the frequencies of the categories strictly falling under that boundary condition.
